summary: A light, tidy worker-placement game where each of your three workers per round vacuums up resources from the eight adjacent tiles, letting you construct buildings that fuel your engine or that opponents can also use if they pay you a toll. Games move briskly over four rounds, with scoring coming from a mix of building powers, constructed buildings, and secret goal cards dealt at the start.
praised: Clean, elegant core mechanism where placing a worker grabs resources from all eight surrounding spaces
The toll system for using rivals' buildings adds a neat, low-friction layer of interaction
Short, brisk playtime (about 30-45 minutes) for the amount of engine-building it offers
Charming, colorful production and easy-to-teach rules make it a solid gateway/family-weight pick
criticised: Can feel like parallel solitaire in lower player counts since direct conflict is limited to space-blocking and tolls
Secret goal cards introduce a luck-of-the-draw element some feel outweighs strategic play
Limited long-term replayability once the building set and strategies are explored
Iconography and building effects can require some upfront explanation despite the simple core loop

interaction.kind: blocking and area denial, plus toll payments when using others' buildings

scoring.why: Points accumulate from building powers used over the game, buildings you've constructed, and how well you complete your secret goal cards.
